cues.zh: 但这仍然热到不能接触任何壁面，否则会损坏材料。为防止这种情况，我们用磁场贯穿整台机器，让高温燃料、高温聚变燃料等离子体远离壁面。但我们在这里做的相当独特：我们接着取初始磁场，通过以极高强度脉冲，每个线圈超过10万安培，

cues.zh: 我们反转该磁场，将磁能困在闭合场中。这被称为自组合、自组织等离子体。

cues.en: topology, a closed plasma object that we can do things to, we can actually do work on. And so at that point, we now have a closed field reverse configuration

It accelerates that plasma out of the formation section, which had all the complex ionization, gas injection, and all those things into higher field section. At this point, we've now moved into what we call the acceleration section or plasma injector, where literally here, we are now continuing to accelerate this plasma to over a million miles an hour, 300 kilometers a second and higher down down the the length of the system.
cues.zh: 对它们进行时序控制。随着我们往下走，它们被依次触发。我们称之为蠕动加速，就像挤一管牙膏一样。它把等离子体从形成段加速出去——那里有复杂的电离、气体注入等等——送入更高场强的区段。此时，我们进入了所谓的加速段或等离子体注入器，在这里，我们继续把这团等离子体加速到每小时超过一百万英里，即每秒300公里甚至更高，沿着整个系统的长度往下推进。

cues.zh: 氘

You compress the fuel, it begins to burn, it then gets hotter, it pushes back on that piston, only we do it all electromagnetically.
cues.zh: 与氦-3 聚变，形成氦-4 和一个额外的氢。现在这两个粒子温度都非常高。它们诞生在聚变等离子体内部，反过来对这些磁场施加压力。这就像活塞一样：在活塞里，你压缩燃料，它开始燃烧，然后变得更热，再反推活塞，只不过我们这一切都是通过电磁方式完成的。

cues.en: This is a truly innovative concept.
cues.zh: 这是一个真正创新的概念。

cues.en: With tokamak reactors, like the massive ITER reactor being built in France right now,
cues.zh: 对于托卡马克反应堆，比如目前正在法国建造的大型ITER反应堆，

cues.en: Electricity is created by converting the kinetic energy of neutrons expelled during fusion to heat, by slowing them down in the blanket walls. This heat is then transferred to high pressure water to create high pressure steam,
cues.zh: 电力是通过将聚变过程中释放的中子的动能转化为热量来产生的，方法是在包层壁中减慢这些中子。然后，这种热量被传递给高压水，产生高压蒸汽，

cues.en: which turns a turbine attached to electric generator that rapidly rotates a magnetic field around copper wires to generate an electric current.
cues.zh: 蒸汽驱动连接在发电机上的涡轮机，发电机使磁场在铜线周围快速旋转，从而产生电流。

cues.en: Helion is skipping steps one through four and going straight to moving a magnetic field around copper wires.
cues.zh: Helion跳过了第一到第四步，直接让磁场在铜线周围移动。

cues.en: Generating electricity directly from the magnetic field cradling the fusion reaction at the center of the machine.
cues.zh: 直接从环绕机器中心聚变反应的磁场中发电。

cues.en: As the fusion reaction occurs,
cues.zh: 当聚变反应发生时，

cues.en: the energy it generates begins to push back on the magnetic field confining it, moving it. As David said, like a piston. It's this changing magnetic field that will generate helium's electricity.
cues.zh: 它产生的能量开始反推约束它的磁场，使其移动。正如David所说，就像活塞一样。正是这个变化的磁场将产生Helion的电力。

cues.en: Skipping all the initial steps needed to boil water and turn a turbine should,
cues.zh: 跳过烧水和转动涡轮机所需的所有初始步骤，

cues.en: in theory, make it vastly more efficient.
cues.zh: 理论上应该能使其效率大大提高。

cues.en: While also unlocking the major benefits of a superior nuclear fusion fuel mixture.
cues.zh: 同时还解锁了更优的核聚变燃料混合物带来的主要优势。

cues.en: One of the problems with tokamak reactors is their choice of fuels.
cues.zh: 托卡马克反应堆的问题之一在于燃料的选择。

cues.en: The fuel mixture of choice for tokamaks is deuterium and tritium.
cues.zh: 托卡马克首选燃料混合物是氘和氚。

cues.en: The availability of deuterium is not a problem, it's everywhere.
cues.zh: 氘的可用性不是问题，它无处不在。

cues.en: This is a bottle of heavy water, water with two deuterium atoms instead of two regular hydrogen atoms.
cues.zh: 这是一瓶重水，水里的两个普通氢原子被换成了两个氘原子。

cues.en: It's cheap and safe.
cues.zh: 它便宜又安全。

cues.en: I can even drink it. However, tritium as we spoke about in more detail in our last video is extremely rare.
cues.zh: 我甚至能喝它。不过，正如我们上个视频里更详细讲过的，氚极其稀有。

cues.en: We only have about 20 kilograms of it in global reserves and a single commercial scale tokamak is expected to burn through 300 grams of it a day. Giving us about two months of operation with the worlds entire current supply.
cues.zh: 全球储备只有约20公斤，而一座商业规模的托卡马克预计每天要消耗300克。也就是说，用全球现有全部储备只够运行约两个月。

cues.en: Tokamak generators will manufacture tritium on-site
cues.zh: 托卡马克发电机将在现场制造氚

cues.en: using a lithium breeding layer. When the high neutrons
cues.zh: 使用锂增殖层。当那些高能中子

cues.en: from our nuclear fusion reaction collide with the lithium in the reactor wall, the lithium splits into tritium and helium.
cues.zh: 从核聚变反应中射出，并与反应堆壁里的锂碰撞时，锂会分裂成氚和氦。

cues.en: This is a reasonable solution,
cues.zh: 这是个合理的方案，

cues.en: but 80% of the energy of the tritium deuterium fusion reaction is carried by those high energy neutrons.
cues.zh: 但氚氘聚变反应中，80%的能量由这些高能中子携带。

cues.en: So we have effectively wasted
cues.zh: 所以实际上我们浪费了

cues.en: all of our energy to get back to square one.
cues.zh: 所有能量，结果又回到原点。

cues.en: To combat this, the first layer of tokamak walls will be made of beryllium,
cues.zh: 为了解决这个问题，托卡马克壁的第一层将用铍制成，

cues.en: a neutron multiplier,
cues.zh: 一种中子倍增剂，

cues.en: which creates two neutrons when struck by one neutron.
cues.zh: 它被一个中子击中时会产生两个中子。

cues.en: Giving us one neutron to create tritium and one neutron to generate heat.
cues.zh: 这样一个中子用来制造氚，另一个中子用来产生热量。

cues.en: However,
cues.zh: 然而，

cues.en: beryllium is extremely expensive.
cues.zh: 铍极其昂贵。

cues.en: The entire annual global supply is just enough to build a single tokamak generator.
cues.zh: 全球全年总供应量只够造一座托卡马克发电机。

cues.en: Beryllium also contains uranium impurities

cues.zh: 每个单元都是？每个盒子都是一个电容器，能储存几千焦耳的能量。然后我们有几百个这样的电容器，以模块化的方式并联起来，组成主电池组。

cues.en: In parallel to that are other capacitors that are slower response, higher efficiency. Those are run with semiconductor switches,
cues.zh: 与此同时，还有其他电容器，它们响应较慢、效率更高。这些由半导体开关驱动，

cues.zh: 可能有 20 个吧

cues.zh: 我们用于某些形成段、某些注入器以及初始电离段的旧设备。

cues.zh: 稍后你们在我们的设施，埃弗雷特的Antares设施里，会看到我们新的电容器生产线，我们在那里制造专为这一应用设计的定制电容器。

cues.en: And those outperform even the older technology.

cues.zh: 仅仅

cues.zh: 当你达到更快的脉冲时，这些随着时间推移可能会退化，这速率有问题吗，还是？

cues.en: Yeah. So one one of the keys to these systems is as you're running them, what we call repetition rate, where you're pulsing not once every ten minutes like Trenta does, but where you're pulsing every ten seconds or once a second or 10 times a second. Now the lifetime of the capacitors, their ability to handle throughput, average throughput, and the heating in the capacitor starts to become engineering issues that we have to consider.
cues.zh: 是的。这些系统的关键之一在于，当你运行它们时，我们称之为重复率，你不是像Trenta那样每十分钟脉冲一次，而是每十秒脉冲一次，或每秒一次，或每秒10次。那么电容器的寿命、它们处理吞吐量、平均吞吐量的能力，以及电容器内的发热，就开始成为我们必须考虑的工程问题。

cues.en: Luckily,
cues.zh: 幸运的是，

cues.en: as we've evolved, so has the capacitor technology, and so self healing and other capacitors that have long life, maybe not pulsed, but are long life, those capacitor technologies are now enabling for
cues.zh: 随着我们的演进，电容器技术也在演进，所以自愈和其他长寿命的电容器——也许不是脉冲的，但寿命长——那些电容器技术现在正使能

cues.en: subscale systems, not on Trenta, but Trenta has done over 10,000
cues.zh: 亚规模系统，不是在Trenta上，但Trenta已经完成了超过10,000次

cues.en: high power pulses doing fusion.
cues.zh: 高功率脉冲进行聚变。

cues.en: In some of our subscale systems that we did earlier, weren't doing fusion but were making these types of plasmas, We've done not not tens of thousands, but we've done billions of discharges with capacitors and run them steady for months on end at hundreds of hertz. So we have a lot of experience in building steady operating pulse power systems that are quite a bit smaller than this. And so a lot of the work we have now is taking those experiences and that engineering
cues.zh: 在我们早期的一些子尺度系统中，虽然没做聚变，但也在制造这类等离子体。我们不是做了数万次，而是用电容器完成了数十亿次放电，并以数百赫兹的频率连续稳定运行了数月。所以我们在建造稳定运行的脉冲功率系统方面有大量经验，而且规模比这个小得多。因此，我们现在很多工作就是把这些经验，以及我们在 Helion 积累的工程

cues.en: experience that we have at Helion and and combining that with the large scale pulse power fusion systems and merging those together into the Polaris system. With the size of this capacitor bank you would think it holds an astounding amount of energy,
cues.zh: 经验，与大规模脉冲功率聚变系统结合起来，融合到 Polaris 系统中。看这个电容器组的规模，你会以为它储存的能量大得惊人，

cues.en: but the total capacity of the bank is just 10,000,000 joules,
cues.zh: 但这个电容组的总容量只有 10,000,000 焦耳，

cues.en: the equivalent energy of about 22 bananas.
cues.zh: 大约相当于 22 根香蕉的能量。

cues.en: Or in terms of a typical tesla battery pack, that's 2.8
cues.zh: 或者按典型的特斯拉电池包来算，是 2.8

cues.en: kilowatt hours,
cues.zh: 千瓦时，

cues.en: one thirtieth the capacity of a typical tesla battery.
cues.zh: 是典型特斯拉电池容量的三十分之一。

cues.en: However, we aren't expending that energy in an hour. We are releasing it in one hundred microseconds.
cues.zh: 不过，我们不是在一小时内释放这些能量，而是在一百微秒内释放。

cues.en: These capacitors release a lightning bolt of current through the machine. Gigawatts of instantaneous

cues.en: power.
But it isn't an uncontrolled burst of electricity like a lightning bolt.
cues.zh: 但这不是像闪电那样不受控制的电流爆发。

cues.en: It's a carefully controlled orchestra of switches.
cues.zh: 而是一支精心控制的开关交响乐。

cues.en: Releasing and controlling this much electricity with microsecond
cues.zh: 以微秒级

cues.en: precision
cues.zh: 精度

cues.en: simply was not possible when the concept was first envisioned.
cues.zh: 释放并控制这么大的电量，在这个概念最初被提出时根本不可能做到。

cues.en: Within those one hundred microseconds,
cues.zh: 在这一百微秒之内，

cues.en: thousands of operations occur across the machine.
cues.zh: 整台机器上会发生数千次操作。

cues.en: Each row of electromagnets
cues.zh: 每一排电磁铁

cues.en: along the machine need to activate three hundred nanoseconds
cues.zh: 都需要在前一排之后三百纳秒

cues.en: after the previous.
cues.zh: 依次激活。

cues.en: They need to trigger just as the plasma passes by,
cues.zh: 它们必须在等离子体经过的瞬间触发，

cues.en: traveling at millions of kilometers per hour to push it even faster towards the center.
cues.zh: 以每小时数百万公里的速度推动它更快地冲向中心。

cues.zh: 没有现代微处理器

cues.zh: 即便如此，Helion 还必须考虑光在玻璃光纤中的传播速度、

cues.zh: 电流通过微型半导体开关所需的时间，以及系统中其他所有延迟。

cues.zh: Helion 现在做的事情令人惊叹。

cues.zh: 将两个等离子体环推入剧烈碰撞，并在中心的磁阱中捕获这次碰撞，

cues.en: Overcoming one of the universe's strongest forces to create new elements in the belly of a man made machine.
cues.zh: 克服宇宙中最强大的力之一，在人造机器的腹中创造新元素。

cues.en: Capturing the energy of the expanding plasma to generate electricity.
cues.zh: 捕获膨胀等离子体的能量来发电。

cues.en: Adding even more complexity to the delicate symphony.
cues.zh: 给这首精妙的交响乐增添更多复杂度。

cues.zh: 能量在电容器组之间来回流动，就像海岸边的潮汐。如果一切按计划进行，希望潮汐的每一次涨落，都能把一种改变世界的电力来源推上我们的电网。
